A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLAP and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably across the appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLAP experiments on GemBench and a real robot, component ablations, and detailed per-task results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds demonstration-count and action-predictor input ablations in Tables 11–12.

M1.justification: The task planner, reasoning procedure, auxiliary training tasks, and fine-grained predictor remain unchanged. The added pixel-to-3D explanation and revised Figure 2 clarify the existing implementation rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GemBench tasks and variations and the same real-world manipulation scenarios. The language-plan, object-position, and trajectory datasets already appear in v1; v2 adds documentation and varies demonstration counts within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The GemBench comparisons retain HiveFormer, PolarNet, 3D Diffuser Actor, RVT2, 3D-LOTUS, 3D-LOTUS++, and BridgeVLA. The real-world comparison remains against RVT2. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments vary training demonstrations across 10, 20, 50, and 100 and compare RGB, RGB+Depth, and the full predictor inputs. Existing benchmark protocols and the hyperparameters in v1 Table 5, now v2 Table 6, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 supplements the retained Table 2 ablations with two targeted analyses: sensitivity to demonstration count and the contribution of depth and 3D positional inputs. These extend evidence about data efficiency and representation choices within the existing system.

E5.justification: Tables 11–12 specify three runs with different random seeds and report uncertainty for overall averages, including 62.0 ± 0.5 for the full configuration. The original five-seed evaluation statement remains; the PDFs do not establish increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Existing result tables are unchanged. Table 11 adds average success rates of 60.0, 61.1, and 61.0 for 10, 50, and 100 demonstrations, respectively. Table 12 adds 60.9 for RGB and 60.8 for RGB+Depth, alongside the full configuration's retained 62.0.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(4) are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs appear; the added coordinate-mapping sentence is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same generalization and sample-efficiency claims, including the GemBench advantage using one-fifth of the trajectories and real-world generalization with ten demonstrations per task.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an explanation attributing trajectory efficiency partly to auxiliary language-plan and object-position data supplying planning and grounding capabilities. The existing limitations concerning unstructured tasks and missing error correction remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 4 newly document plan augmentation, scene and trajectory transformations, and training/validation sample counts. The reproducibility statement replaces a future code-release promise with a repository pointer. Hardware, training times, and listed hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds GRAVMAD and DeCo to the related-work citations and bibliography without substantially revising its positioning. BridgeVLA and SAM 2 receive publication-reference updates, rather than being newly introduced works.

P1.justification: v2 adds short methodological clarifications, appendix cross-references, training-data and additional-ablation subsections, acknowledgments, and conference headers. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 redraws the predictor panel to show the encoders and positional embedding explicitly. v2 adds three tables for sample counts and ablations and rearranges existing appendix displays, including Figure 4. The remaining figures and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through training-data construction details, sample counts, and code-access information. The new ablations provide focused evidence about demonstration efficiency and predictor inputs, while Figure 2 explains the implementation more clearly. These are useful, limited gains over v1; the main method, benchmark results, and central claims remain unchanged.
